'''Oyreain''', officially the '''Republic of Oyreain''', is a country in [[West Massir]] and on the [[Ayre archipelago]], between the [[Southern Eanif Ocean|Southern Eanif]] and [[Vihsanna ocean|Vihsanna oceans]]. Comprising over [[Islands of Oyreain|2,000 islands,]] including [[Shuese]], [[Miwa]], [[Robliyye]], and many smaller islands, Oyreain is on the [[Largest archipelagos|world's second-largest archipelago]] and the 83rd-largest country by area, at [[List of countries and dependencies by area|209,781 square kilometres]] (80,997 square miles). With over 31 million people, Oyreain is the world's [[List of countries and dependencies by population|fourth-fifth-most-populous country]] and home to the [[Yogito]] religion. [[Shuese]], the world's fourth [[Most Populated island|most populous island]], is home to more than 80% of the country's population.

Oyreain operates as a presidential republic with an elected legislature and consists of [[Provinces of Oyreain|22 provinces]], 5 of which have special autonomous status. Yemboto is the [[List of largest cities|largest city]] and capital of the nation. Oyreain does not share land borders with any other nation; it has maritime borders with [[Dahe]], [[Cloja]], [[North Ayre]] and [[Sanagara]]. Despite its small size and densely populated regions, Oyreain has vast areas of wilderness that support one of the world's highest levels of biodiversity.

The [[Ayre archipelago]] has been a valuable region for trade since at least the sixth century, when [[Robliyye|Robliyye's]] [[Miran Empire]] and later [[Shuese|Shuese's]] [[Chiurvue Kingdoms]] engaged in commerce with entities from mainland [[Massir]], [[New Ayre]], to [[Taval]]. Over the centuries, local rulers assimilated foreign influences, leading to the flourishing of ____ and _____ kingdoms. [[Taval|Tavalan]] traders and [[Wikipedia:Scholar|scholars]] later brought ____, and [[Ayuma|Ayuman powers]] fought one another to monopolise trade in the Spice Islands of [[Sokato Islands|Sokato]] during the 13th century. Following one and a half centuries of [[Taval|Tavalan]] trade dominance, the [[Ayuma|Ayuman]] powers, undergoing industrialisation, overtook Taval in influence throughout the region. During the 16th and 17th centuries, [[Siana]] colonised the islands. Following the [[Dahe|Dahen]] invasion during the [[Red War]], the [[Oyreain Independence|islands declared independence]]; however, [[Siana]] reasserted control after the war. This led to a [[Oyreain insurgency|15-year guerrilla insurgency]] by local forces. Oyreain's [[Oyreain Independence|independence was officially recognised]] in 1717, following the [[Sinian Revolution]] in 1716 and the [[Nuclear bombing of Minalu]] in 1717, after which Siana withdrew from the islands. Since independence, Oyreain has experienced challenges including [[Separatist movements in Oyreain|separatist movements,]], political corruption, and natural disasters, alongside periods of democratisation and significant economic growth.

Oyreain society comprises hundreds of [[Ethnic groups in Oyreain|ethnic and linguistic groups]], with [[Oyreain peoples|Oyreain]] being the largest. The nation's identity is unified under a nationalist idea of throwing off the oppressors, defined by a national language, cultural and religious pluralism, a history of colonialism, and rebellion against it. A newly industrialised country, Oyreain's economy ranks as the world's [[List of countries by GDP (nominal)|42nd-largest by nominal GDP]] a. A minor power in global affairs, the country is a member of several multilateral organisations, including the [[EISA]], the [[Massiran Economic fund|Massiran Economic fund,]] the [[Global Development Bank]], and the [[Global Trade Union]]. It is a member of [[SDSA]] and a founding member of the [[LLO]] and the [[Massiran Summit]]. Yemboto is also the headquarters of the [[Association of Ayre Nations]]
